topics.summary: The client sends one framed command over one IPv4 loopback connection and prints the response. A syntactically received application error is printed as a response; scripts must inspect that response rather than assuming every zero client exit means a job succeeded.

reading.title: 28.1.1 Assigning Responsibilities to the Client, Gateway, and Worker
paragraphs: The client sends one framed command over one IPv4 loopback connection and prints the response. It has a finite exchange budget and does not automatically create new job identities or retry mutations. A transport failure produces an error exit. A syntactically received application error is printed as a response; scripts must inspect that response rather than assuming every zero client exit means a job succeeded.

The gateway validates submission syntax, commits accepted intent, serves status, and runs a dispatcher for pending jobs. Its API handler and dispatcher use separate SQLite connections to the same file. Its counters are in memory and reset after restart; its jobs remain in the database.

The worker validates execution requests and commits a receipt containing key, input, and result. The domain result is the square of an integer in the closed range zero through one million. This makes the maximum result one trillion, within the chosen signed 64-bit representation, and gives the gateway an exact inexpensive validation oracle.

topics.title: 28.1.2 Enumerating Limits and Unsupported Promises
topics.summary: Payloads are bounded at 4096 bytes. Keys contain one to 64 permitted ASCII characters. Each server admits at most 64 simultaneous peer connections and accepts at most 16 new connections in one reactor iteration. A connection has a two-second cooperative lifetime; the poll loop wakes periodically to inspect state and stop requests.

blocks.text: The gateway accepts at most 128 currently pending unique jobs by default. Duplicate submissions with unchanged meaning remain recognizable when that limit is reached. Completed rows and receipts are not pruned, so disk growth is not fully bounded by the pending limit.

blocks.text: The dispatcher selects batches of at most 16 pending jobs and gives each worker exchange a 200 ms budget. These are teaching choices. A synchronous database operation or ordinary scheduler delay can extend observed wall time beyond a simple sum of nominal timers. There is no hard-real-time guarantee.

blocks.text: The reactor handles partial socket I/O, but handlers execute synchronously. Moving to an asynchronous database adapter would require explicit operation lifetime and completion ownership. Calling the current server “nonblocking” should refer to its socket mechanism, not imply that every dependency is asynchronous.

topics.summary: If the gateway stops after acceptance, its pending row remains. If the worker commits and drops its reply, the dispatcher retries and retrieves the retained result. If the gateway receives a result but stops before recording completion, replay again retrieves the same receipt.

reading.title: Engineering case — Choose one extension and preserve the reference contract
paragraphs: Suppose the next project replaces the custom framed transport with gRPC. The goal is not to redesign every layer at once. Keep the domain request, canonicalization, store transaction, and duplicate result semantics unchanged while introducing the new adapter.

Define a schema whose fields preserve the key and integer meaning. Map application outcomes explicitly: accepted, conflict, capacity rejection, invalid input, pending, and completed. Decide which are domain response fields and which are transport status codes. Do not encode a successful business conflict as an unstructured exception that clients retry blindly.

The adapter must carry deadlines and cancellation according to the framework’s documented behavior, but durable acceptance still outlives a caller’s wait by design. A gRPC cancellation does not erase a committed pending row. Tests should retain the lost-response and restart histories under the new transport rather than replacing them with only a hello-world RPC.

Generated schema sources, runtime versions, and TLS credentials introduce new build and operational requirements. Keep the original loopback client as a reference path until semantic equivalence is established. The optional .proto file in this package is a starting contract exercise, not a prevalidated implementation of that adapter.

A second possible extension is persistent terminal failure and redrive. It changes the gateway state machine and schema rather than the transport. It needs a reason code, attempt metadata, an authorized redrive identity, and rules for preserving the original worker key. Reusing a new key during redrive could duplicate an effect that merely had an uncertain reply.

Choose one extension, write its invariant and migration plan, and add tests at the boundary it changes. Combining gRPC, sharding, new computation semantics, and receipt pruning in one revision makes failures difficult to attribute and rollback difficult to reason about.

The capstone’s value is that it provides a small executable reference whose assumptions are explicit. Extend it by replacing one assumption with a stronger tested mechanism, not by accumulating frameworks around an undocumented core.
